title: Prompt Library Governance: Versioning, Ownership, and Retirement (2026)

questions.question: Who may move a PromptRecord from DRAFT to REVIEW?
options: Any reviewer, because REVIEW is only an editorial state
The decision owner, even when the record owner is absent
The registered owner, because can_promote requires acting_as to match owner
The model provider, because it controls the target model
questions.explanation: The DRAFT-to-REVIEW transition is valid only when acting_as equals record.owner. The owner submits the prompt; an independent reviewer is required for the later STABLE transition.

questions.question: Why is support-ticket-summariser blocked when first promoted from REVIEW to STABLE?
options: Its anchor score of 0.87 is below the default 0.80 threshold
The transition REVIEW -> STABLE is not allowed in VALID_TRANSITIONS
The prompt has no owner, so it cannot be placed in REVIEW
Its reviewer equals its owner, so self-review is not permitted
questions.explanation: The transition and 0.87 anchor are valid, but reviewer='cx-automation' equals owner='cx-automation'. can_promote blocks the self-review before the prompt can become STABLE.

questions.question: What allows contract-clause-extractor to become STABLE after its reviewer is set to risk-and-compliance?
options: The reviewer differs from the owner and its anchor score 0.92 clears the 0.80 threshold
The model sunset rule bypasses the promotion gate
A prompt can become STABLE directly from DRAFT when its version is 1.2.0
The owner and reviewer are intentionally identical for legal prompts
questions.explanation: The prompt is already in REVIEW, has an anchor at 0.92, and now has an independent reviewer. Those conditions satisfy the REVIEW-to-STABLE gate.

questions.question: What does can_promote return when keyword-intent-classifier in STABLE is asked to move directly to REVIEW?
options: True, because a review is safer than a retirement
False with an invalid-transition reason; STABLE may move only to DEPRECATED
True, because its anchor score is below the accuracy floor
False only if a replacement prompt is already stable
questions.explanation: VALID_TRANSITIONS permits STABLE -> DEPRECATED, not STABLE -> REVIEW. can_promote rejects the request before checking owner, reviewer, or anchor conditions.

questions.question: Why does apply_retirement_rules retire support-ticket-summariser in the driver?
options: Its target model is in SUNSET_MODELS
Its date_sunset has passed
Its current accuracy score 0.74 is below its 0.80 accuracy floor
A stable replacement is always required for every support prompt
questions.explanation: The prompt's RetirementRule sets accuracy_floor=0.80, and the current score map gives it 0.74. The evaluator returns that prompt with an accuracy_floor trigger.

questions.question: What redirect does the driver attach when keyword-intent-classifier is retired by its date rule?
options: None; retired prompts are deleted from the registry
support-ticket-summariser
claude-sonnet-4-6
neural-intent-classifier
questions.explanation: The date-sunset rule retires keyword-intent-classifier, and the driver sets its tombstone_redirect to neural-intent-classifier. The tombstone preserves a safe caller handoff instead of silently dropping requests.
